jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Full-time | Hybrid | San Francisco, CA

https://firstgraduate.org/careers/

https://firstgraduate.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Final-First-Graduate-ED-Position-Description.pdf

The Opportunity
First Graduate stands ready for our next chapter of growth and impact. We're seeking an
Executive Director who can both strengthen our organizational infrastructure and champion our
mission externally — someone who is equally comfortable managing budgets and building
donor relationships, overseeing daily operations, and inspiring community partners.
Our ideal candidate brings deep nonprofit operational experience, proven fundraising success,
and authentic passion for educational equity, understanding that sustainable impact requires
both exceptional programs and the resources to deliver them. They're energized by building
relationships with donors and partners, know how to translate a mission into a narrative that
inspires investment, and can think strategically about the next three to five years of growth.
If you're a nonprofit leader called to make a measurable impact on educational equity in San
Francisco, this is your opportunity to lead transformational change. This position offers the rare
opportunity to lead an organization with a 25-year track record of proven impact, a committed
team and board, and tremendous growth potential. The incoming Executive Director inherits an
organization performing at the top of its field, with real growth underway. Our model has been
refined and validated through decades of success, and SFUSD partners are actively requesting
our services at additional schools. The momentum this leader will build on includes:
● 690 youth are currently served across the middle school, high school, and college &
career continuum, up from 300 the year prior
● 99% of seniors graduate from high school and enroll in college immediately, compared
to a 46% national average for first-generation students
● 78% of First Graduate students complete a four-year degree within six years of enrolling
— more than three times the national completion rate for first-generation students
● Expanding into a new middle school (Visitacion Valley) and a new high school in-school
advising partnership (Lowell), with high school enrollment projected to nearly double
year-over-year
● A growing career pipeline, anchored by a partnership with Deloitte and $239,200 in
scholarships awarded annually
● 11 new corporate and foundation funders added over the past three years, diversifying
the organization's funding base

Key Responsibilities
This is a hands-on role split roughly evenly between internal operations and external
relationship building. Fundraising and relationship building are central to this role. The Executive
Director is expected to be personally and visibly engaged in resource development and external
partnerships.

Organizational Leadership & Operations (~50%)
● Serve as chief executive, ensuring strong execution across programs, finance, operations,
and people management
● Lead a team of 13-20, fostering professional development and a culture of accountability
and collaboration
● Build and sustain an inclusive, high-performing culture where staff feel valued,
supported, and set up to grow
● Own budgeting, forecasting, and financial management with the finance committee and
Board, ensuring fiscal health and strong internal controls
● Ensure compliance with nonprofit governance, labor law, and reporting requirements,
and proactively manage organizational risk
● Strengthen internal systems and processes to support operational excellence and growth
● Ensure programs are delivered with quality, consistency, and measurable impact
● Serve as primary liaison to the Board, providing regular updates on financial
performance, fundraising progress, and organizational health
● Partner with the Board on strategic planning, governance, and board
development/recruitment

Development & External Relations (~50%)
● Serve as the organization's lead fundraiser, personally cultivating, soliciting, and
stewarding major donors, foundations, and institutional funders
● Develop and execute a fundraising strategy supporting a ~$2.5M annual budget
● Partner with the Board to activate members as fundraisers and ambassadors
● Maintain high-quality stewardship and reporting for existing funders
● Identify and pursue new funding opportunities aligned with long-term sustainability
● Serve as First Graduate's primary external spokesperson, building relationships with
school partners, community organizations, and education leaders across the Bay Area
● Increase organizational visibility through strategic outreach, storytelling, and
communications

Qualifications & Experience
Required
● Genuine passion for educational equity and First Graduate's mission
● High emotional intelligence, integrity, and authenticity, with a relationship-driven
leadership style
● Bachelor's degree and 8-10+ years of nonprofit leadership experience, with significant
operational and management responsibility
● Demonstrated experience managing organizations or departments with budgets, ideally
in the $2M+ range and teams of 10+ staff
● Proven track record of personally leading fundraising efforts, including major donor and
institutional funder relationships
● Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, and managing restricted
funds
● Experience working closely with and supporting a nonprofit Board of Directors
● Experience scaling programs, revenue, and organizational impact, with comfort
navigating complexity and change
● Inclusive, equity-driven leadership style, with a track record of developing, retaining, and
motivating diverse teams
Preferred Qualifications
● Background in education, youth development, or college access
● Experience with K-12 school systems
● Familiar with the San Francisco nonprofit/philanthropic community
● Capital campaign or major gifts fundraising experience

Our Team: Culture and Benefits
First Graduate is committed to cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and
connectedness. We grow and learn better together with a diverse team of employees. The
collective sum of the individual differences, life experiences, knowledge, innovation,
self-expression, and talent that our employees bring is an important part of our culture. In
recruiting for our team, we welcome the unique contributions that you can bring in terms of
your education, opinions, culture, ethnicity, race, sex, gender identity and expression, nation of
origin, age, languages spoken, veteran status, color, religion, disability, sexual orientation, and
beliefs.
We back that commitment with a total rewards package designed to support our team well: a
salary range of $170,000-$200,000; generous vacation, personal days, paid holidays, and sick
leave; comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with 100% employer-paid premiums
for employees; a 403(b) retirement plan; life insurance, an Employee Assistance Program, and
short- and long-term disability coverage. We also provide dedicated funds for ongoing
professional development and growth.

How to Apply
Please submit a thoughtful cover letter and resume to: Susannah Sallin, Search Consultant to
Nonprofits at apply@sallinsearch.com with "First Graduate Executive Director" in the subject
line. We will respond to all applicants. Thank you.

jobs.title: VP of Operations / COO
jobs.description:
About age1

First as The Longevity Fund and since 2023 as age1, we back founders at the earliest stages of building therapeutics, tools, and technologies that increase healthy lifespan. We partner closely with scientists and operators to turn frontier ideas into category-first companies defining the field. Counterfactual impact is a large north star of ours.

We’re a small team with a deeply embedded network and an ambitious mandate: fund the best longevity companies, build the community and talent base the field needs, and do both with a level of rigor and follow-through the category has historically lacked.

About the Role

We are hiring a VP of Operations/COO  to manage operations for age1, which includes legacy Longevity Fund vehicles. The COO role is likely on track to become a Partner on a 1-2 year timeline.

The ideal candidate has worked in an operational role at a fast-paced startup for 5-10+ years, or equivalently significant operating experience, ideally but not necessarily including experience operating with a venture fund. The team is currently distributed globally with hubs in San Francisco and Boston. We have a strong preference for on-site, but are open to hybrid/remote arrangements.

Key Responsibilities

You will own fund operations, fundraising, investor relations, portfolio support, community, finance, firm strategy, and the internal operating system that runs the firm. The right person has stood up and led operating systems in a startup or investment firm before, has the confidence to push back on the partners to shape firm-level decisions, and can move between closing an LP, setting the quarter’s priorities with the partners, and running a founder event in the same week.

Investor Relations
Drive the operations of the fund's next raise. Own the operational process end to end - pipeline, data room preparation, diligence requests, meeting prep, and follow-up.
Bring in new investor leads through one-on-one meetings and events, and keep every conversation and commitment tracked so nothing gets lost.
Proactively deepen relationships with existing LPs, and lead the writing of investor updates that are clear and concise. 

Financial Operations
Manage internal age1 operations team and part-time operational support such as CFO/fund admin, tax advisors, audit, payroll, subscriptions, etc.
Report firm performance to the relevant databases on an ongoing basis.
Oversee all financial planning, analysis, forecasting, and budgeting.
Ensure end-to-end finance support across the fund lifecycle and portfolio deal activity

Portfolio Relationship Management
Own the relationships and ongoing communication with portfolio companies.
Lead the growth of age1’s platform for portfolio support - helping founders hire, raise subsequent rounds, and access the resources and networks that give them an edge. Build repeatable programs founders across the portfolio can draw on.

Sourcing, Diligence, and Community
Lead the firm’s community efforts, own the CRM, and support sourcing. This can take many forms: spearhead media, curate and host events, or plan a founder program/fellowship. 
Support the investment team in making efficient, maximally-informed decisions, with an emphasis on portfolio construction and modeling. 
Find and build the non-obvious paths to activate age1’s network with outsized impact.  For a path towards Partner, build a track record of contributing directly to investment decisions, with an emphasis on portfolio construction and modeling.

Incubations
Help lead company formation for NewCo incubations in their 0 to 1 phase, owning set-up of operational platforms: entity registration, standing up finances, establishing governance, etc.
Help drive negotiation of key agreements linked to the NewCo’s vision for assets or partnerships (investment terms, legal documents, and BD/transactions).
Help set NewCo vision, and on a path toward Partner, build a track record in contributing to the recruitment of key founding hires plus the production of fundraising materials (e.g., NewCo deck).

Fund Strategy
Contribute to setting fund priorities and high-level firm initiatives alongside the partners.
Shape how the firm allocates time, capital, and attention as it scales.

Team Growth and Firm Operations
Work with the partners to set and execute team development goals.
Manage the physical office, website, public relations, and community events; own the recruiting process for summer interns and fellows.

Attributes We're Looking For

You have a great read on people . Building community, you know exactly who to route to the partners. With LPs, co-investors, and portfolio companies, you have a sharp instinct for what they need and how they're feeling.
Operational excellence: nothing drops . You cross the t's and dot the i's without being asked. Things don’t slip despite every best intention of the GP’s chaos. You keep the trains running on time with little oversight, and you're skilled at managing up.
You build systems with judgment, not just to-do lists . You've owned complex, cross-functional work with minimal existing infrastructure and turned informal processes into things that scale. You can make the call without waiting for detailed instructions.
No job is beneath you or above you, uninteresting, or out of your abilities . You are happy subbing in wherever the firm needs it, and you don't see logistical execution as separate from senior operating work. You like organizing events (even if it means last minute Uber Eats-ing drinks or a whiteboard) and you don’t mind supporting portfolio companies with ops, such as helping them file documents or set up payroll.
You’re financially fluent . Budgeting, forecasting, and management reporting are comfortable territory, and you can hold your own on fund mechanics.
You write well . You produce concise, high-quality materials for investors, founders, and senior stakeholders, and you default to clear written communication.
You can push back . Low ego, high confidence, and high integrity - you execute the partners' vision and you have the conviction to tell them when you think they're wrong.
You care about the mission . You have a passion for longevity and biotech, and are invested in the future of the fund.

Why You May Not Be a Fit

You want a narrowly defined role with stable, predictable responsibilities.
You're most comfortable operating inside mature systems someone else built.
You want to advise on operations without being accountable for implementation.
You need frequent partner direction to prioritize and finish work.
You see administrative or logistical execution as beneath a senior operating role.
You add process for its own sake, without asking if it improves speed or judgment.

If you have any questions about the role, please reach out to careers@age1.com.

jobs.title: Senior or Executive Director, Analytical Development CMC
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Iambic Therapeutics is seeking a Senior or Executive Director to lead the analytical development and QC function within CMC. This leadership role will provide scientific, strategic, and operational oversight of Analytical Development and Quality Control activities across Iambic’s small-molecule portfolio, supporting programs from early clinical development through late-stage development and commercialization. The individual will lead phase-appropriate analytical strategies for drug substance and drug product, including analytical method development, transfer and validation, specifications, impurity control, stability, reference standards, product characterization, and release testing. The role will serve as the primary Analytical Development/QC lead for internal cross-functional teams and external CDMOs/testing labs, ensuring high-quality, compliant, and timely execution of analytical activities in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and company procedures.

Key Responsibilities

Lead DS and DP analytical strategy and scientific oversight across characterization, impurity and degradation-product control, reference standards, comparability, and stability, with responsibility for shelf-life/retest assessment and emerging stability risks.
Lead analytical method development, validation, transfer, lifecycle management, and troubleshooting across DS and DP, ensuring methods are fit for purpose, scientifically sound, and aligned with regulatory expectations.
Oversee QC testing and data review for release and stability, including OOS/OOT investigations, deviations, root-cause assessment, CAPAs, and resolution of analytical issues.
Establish scientifically justified specifications and analytical acceptance criteria based on product and process understanding, batch history, stability data, and stage of development.
Provide analytical leadership for dissolution and product-performance testing, including development of QC and discriminatory methods for oral drug products.
Lead the outsourced analytical and QC network, including partner selection, technical oversight, governance, issue resolution, and performance management.
Ensure analytical activities support program timelines and manufacturing readiness through close partnership with Drug Substance, Drug Product, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Clinical Supply, and other cross-functional teams.
Lead analytical CMC support for global regulatory submissions and health authority interactions, including authoring and review of relevant Module 3 content, specifications and justifications, analytical methods, stability sections, and responses to regulatory queries.
Recruit, lead, coach, and develop team members; oversee functional resource planning and budget proposals; and foster a collaborative, high-performing environment aligned with organizational goals.

Qualifications

Ph.D. in Analytical Chemistry or a related field with 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical/Biotech industry (or an M.Sc. with 14+ years or B.Sc. with 17+ years of experience).
Extensive hands-on experience in analytical method development, transfer, troubleshooting, and validation for small molecule drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) across early and late-stage development.
Strong experience developing phase-appropriate analytical control strategies, including specifications, impurity/degradation-product control, reference standards, stability-indicating methods, dissolution, and product characterization.
Demonstrated experience supporting early and late-stage development and regulatory filings, including IND/IMPD and preferably NDA/MAA.
Proven success leading Analytical Development and QC activities through external CDMOs, including technical oversight, issue resolution, and management of multiple programs and partners.
In-depth knowledge of cGMP laboratory operations, global regulatory expectations and relevant ICH guidance.
Strong experience with analytical methods for enabling formulations and conventional oral solid dosage forms.
Proven leadership experience in building collaborative, high-performing teams and working effectively across Drug Substance, Drug Product, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Clinical Supply, and other functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical issues, risks, and recommendations to internal stakeholders, external partners, and health authorities.
Ability to travel up to 15% domestically and internationally.

About Iambic Therapeutics

Iambic is a clinical-stage life-science and technology company developing novel medicines using its AI-driven discovery and development platform. Based in San Diego and founded in 2020, Iambic has assembled a world-class team that unites pioneering AI experts and experienced drug hunters. The Iambic platform has demonstrated delivery of new drug candidates to human clinical trials with unprecedented speed and across multiple target classes and mechanisms of action. Iambic is advancing a pipeline of potential best-in-class and first-in-class clinical assets, both internally and in partnership, to address urgent unmet patient need. Learn more about the Iambic team, platform, pipeline, and partnerships at iambic.ai.

MISSION & CORE VALUES

Our mission is to deliver better medicines through innovations in AI-based discovery technologies. The culture and work at Iambic Therapeutics are profoundly strengthened by the diversity of our people and our differences in background, culture, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, and life experiences. We are committed to building an inclusive environment where a diverse group of talented humans work together to discover therapeutics and create technologies.

Pay And Benefits

We offer industry leading competitive pay, company paid healthcare, flexible spending accounts, voluntary life insurance, 401K matching, and uncapped vacation to our team. We are in a brand-new state-of-the art facility in beautiful San Diego with an onsite gym, dining, and easy access to great places to live and play.

Compensation Range: $224K - $310K

Position is hybrid, and incumbent is required to work a minimum of 3-days per week on site. For more information, please consult the hiring manager.

This position will be working from UCLA Downtown in Downtown LA (433 S. Spring Street, Los Angeles, CA 90013).

Department Summary

Excelling in quality, innovation, and impact, UCLA Extension (UCLAx) is one of the top providers of continuing and professional education in the United States, offering programs and classes to more than 50,000 students per year through approximately 4,500 classes and certificate programs to meet the professional development, continuing education, and personal enrichment needs of the full spectrum of traditional, nontraditional, domestic, international, professional, and continuing education students throughout and beyond Los Angeles.

Position Summary

Shape the future of lifelong learning and workforce development at UCLA Extension.

UCLA Extension seeks a strategic and innovative Program Director for Humanities & Social Sciences
to lead a diverse portfolio spanning Humanities, Social Sciences, Journalism, Creative & Professional Writing, Editing & Publishing, and General Education.

This leadership role will drive portfolio growth, academic excellence, and market relevance by developing programs that connect humanities and social sciences disciplines to emerging workforce needs. The Director will expand pathways in areas such as communication, storytelling, ethical leadership, intercultural competence, civic engagement, critical thinking, and collaborative problem-solving through certificates, microcredentials, and professional education programs.

The successful candidate will advance global learning, foster community and civic engagement, build strategic partnerships, and ensure programs remain competitive and impactful for domestic and international learners. This is a unique opportunity to shape innovative educational experiences that support career success, lifelong learning, and meaningful participation in an increasingly interconnected world.

Key Highlights

Lead strategy, growth, and academic quality for UCLA Extension's Humanities & Social Sciences portfolio.
Develop workforce-aligned programs that translate liberal arts skills into in-demand professional competencies.
Advance global learning, intercultural communication, and workforce readiness.
Drive enrollment, revenue growth, and portfolio sustainability.
Champion civic engagement, public dialogue, and community resilience.
Build partnerships across UCLA, industry, nonprofits, public agencies, and community organizations.
Lead and mentor a high-performing team.
Expand access for diverse, underserved, and international learners.

Salary & Compensation

UCLA provides a full pay range. Actual salary offers consider factors, including budget, prior experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business considerations. Salary offers at the top of the range are not common. Visit UC Benefit package to discover benefits that start on day one, and UC Total Compensation Estimator to calculate the total compensation value with benefits.

Qualifications

7 - 10 years Progressively responsible experience in academic program management or continuing education with demonstrated success leading strategic initiatives and business growth. (Required)
Experience in program design, implementation, and evaluation of continuing education and professional development programs. (Required)
Advanced analytical, problem solving, interpersonal, communication and presentation skills; Excellent oral, written communication and interpersonal skills. (Required)
Experience with outreach to, and programming supports for, underserved communities and students. (Required)
Ability to develop creative continuing education programs within an entrepreneurial framework in response to changing needs and trends; Advanced knowledge of accredited and / or certificate program instruction and delivery methodologies, the organization, market and business strategies. (Required)
Strong communication, interpersonal, and collaborative skills with an ability to relate as peer to faculty, professional associations, community leadership groups, local district, county, and state personnel. Specific strengths in building partnerships. (Required)
Experience in an academic environment; Demonstrates thorough knowledge of the organization's policies and procedures; advanced knowledge of functional area and understands how work impacts UNEX and programs. (Required)
Knowledge and facility with computers, leading word-processing and financial management software within an electronic network office environment. (Required)
Experience or understanding of distance learning methods and techniques for adult education using online learning formats. (Required)
Demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage budgets and projects, and deliver measurable outcomes aligned with institutional goals, including revenue, enrollment, student success, and equity targets. (Required)
Experience managing a budget, fiscal controls, and expenditures. (Required)
Ability to set portfolio level standards for instructional quality and approve instructor pools executed by Program Managers. (Required)
Experience in report writing, proposal and grant writing. (Preferred)

Education, Licenses, Certifications & Personal Affiliations

Bachelor's Degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training (Required) And
Master's Degree degree in relevant field, or equivalent combination of education and relevant industry experience. (Preferred)

Live Scan Background Check: A Live Scan background check must be completed prior to the start of employment.
Age Requirement: Candidate(s) must be 18 years or older to be eligible to be hired.

This means understanding the big picture while also appreciating the day-to-day realities of senior center operations—including staff leadership, programs and activities, facilities, service delivery, community engagement, partnerships, compliance, budgeting, and the experience of the people CCAS serves.

We're looking for a leader who understands that successful aging services are about more than programs on paper.

They're about people, relationships, connection, dignity, independence, and community.

WHY CONVERSE COUNTY?

If you're looking for a place where community still means something, Converse County might be your kind of place.

Douglas and Glenrock offer the best of small-town Wyoming: friendly communities, room to breathe, beautiful scenery, and plenty to do without giving up the convenience of being within reach of larger Wyoming communities.

LOVE THE OUTDOORS?

You're going to have plenty to explore.

Converse County offers opportunities for hiking, fishing, camping, hunting, boating, biking, and simply getting outside.

LOVE HISTORY?

There's plenty of that, too.

Explore historic sites, museums, railroad history, and the many stories of the American West that shaped the area.

HAVE A FAMILY?

Converse County offers parks, walking paths, community events, museums, water activities, and plenty of opportunities to get outside together.

LIKE A LITTLE WYOMING TRADITION?

Douglas is home to the Wyoming State Fair & Rodeo, and the community celebrates its famous jackalope with the kind of small-town personality that makes Wyoming special.

Now About The Job...

We're looking for a leader who can take the big-picture executive view while understanding the details that make senior services and community operations successful.

The Executive Director Will

Provide strategic leadership for Converse County Aging Services and its mission to serve older adults and the community.

Partner with the Board of Directors on governance, organizational strategy, policy, and long-term direction.

Lead, support, and develop the organization's leadership team and staff.

Provide executive oversight of senior center operations in Douglas and Glenrock, including programs, services, facilities, staffing, and community activities.

Ensure senior center programs and services are responsive to the needs of older adults, caregivers, families, and the broader community.

Oversee organizational compliance, risk management, policies, contracts, service agreements, and regulatory requirements.

Work closely with Finance & Administration leadership on budgets, financial reporting, grants, cash flow, internal controls, and long-term financial sustainability.

Support program leadership and promote high-quality, person-centered service delivery.

Help ensure CCAS facilities and senior centers remain safe, welcoming, accessible, and community-focused.

Build strong relationships with community partners, healthcare organizations, local governments, funding agencies, donors, volunteers, businesses, and other stakeholders.

Represent CCAS as a visible and engaged leader throughout Converse County.

Advocate for the needs and interests of older adults and aging communities.

Develop strong organizational systems, processes, and accountability measures.

Identify opportunities to strengthen programs, services, partnerships, funding, and community engagement.

Help position CCAS for long-term growth, sustainability, and continued community impact.

SENIOR CENTER & COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP

This position requires more than traditional administrative leadership.

The Executive Director should understand what it takes to operate a successful senior center and community-based aging services organization.

That Includes Recognizing The Importance Of

Creating welcoming and inclusive senior center environments.

Supporting meaningful programs, activities, meals, social opportunities, and community connections.

Understanding the operational needs of multiple locations.

Supporting staff who work directly with older adults and community members.

Maintaining strong relationships with participants, families, volunteers, and community partners.

Responding to changing demographics and the evolving needs of older adults.

Balancing mission, service quality, financial responsibility, and operational sustainability.

Ensuring CCAS remains a trusted and visible part of the Converse County community.

The right Executive Director will be comfortable moving between boardroom strategy and community connection—from reviewing a budget or grant proposal to visiting a senior center, talking with staff, meeting with community partners, or listening to the people CCAS serves.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR AN EXECUTIVE-LEVEL LEADER

This isn't a position for someone who wants to simply keep the wheels turning.

We're looking for someone who can lead, plan, make decisions, develop people, understand the numbers, manage complexity, strengthen operations, and build relationships.

You Should Bring

Strong executive leadership and communication skills.

Strategic thinking and organizational planning abilities.

Financial literacy and comfort with budgets, financial reports, grants, and organizational finances.

Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills.

Experience leading teams and organizational operations.

Experience with nonprofit, human services, senior services, healthcare, community services, or a related organization is highly valued.

An understanding of senior center operations, aging services, community-based services, or programs serving older adults is preferred.

Excellent relationship-building and community engagement skills.

Professionalism, integrity, accountability, and sound judgment.

A Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Human Services, Gerontology, Social Services, or a related field is preferred, along with 3-5 years of leadership or management experience. Equivalent leadership experience may be considered.

THIS IS A CHANCE TO MAKE A VISIBLE DIFFERENCE

At CCAS, leadership isn't happening somewhere far removed from the people being served.

It's happening in the senior centers, programs, community gatherings, partnerships, conversations, and everyday interactions that help older adults remain connected and engaged.

As Executive Director, you'll have the opportunity to shape an organization that has a direct and visible impact on the people of Converse County.

You'll lead an established community organization while helping determine what aging services and senior center programs should look like for the future.

READY FOR A DIFFERENT KIND OF LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY?

Maybe you're ready to trade traffic for open roads.

Maybe you're ready for a community where people know their neighbors.

Maybe you're looking for a place where your leadership can actually make a difference.

Or maybe you just want to live somewhere you can finish work and be five minutes from wide-open Wyoming.

Whatever brings you here, you'll find an opportunity to lead an organization with a meaningful mission, support senior services and community programs, and become part of a community that values its people.

About age1

First as The Longevity Fund and since 2023 as age1, we back founders at the earliest stages of building therapeutics, tools, and technologies that increase healthy lifespan. We partner closely with scientists and operators to turn frontier ideas into category-first companies defining the field. Counterfactual impact is a large north star of ours.

We’re a small team with a deeply embedded network and an ambitious mandate: fund the best longevity companies, build the community and talent base the field needs, and do both with a level of rigor and follow-through the category has historically lacked.

About the Role

We are hiring a VP of Operations/COO  to manage operations for age1, which includes legacy Longevity Fund vehicles. The COO role is likely on track to become a Partner on a 1-2 year timeline.

The ideal candidate has worked in an operational role at a fast-paced startup for 5-10+ years, or equivalently significant operating experience, ideally but not necessarily including experience operating with a venture fund. The team is currently distributed globally with hubs in San Francisco and Boston. We have a strong preference for on-site, but are open to hybrid/remote arrangements.

Key Responsibilities

You will own fund operations, fundraising, investor relations, portfolio support, community, finance, firm strategy, and the internal operating system that runs the firm. The right person has stood up and led operating systems in a startup or investment firm before, has the confidence to push back on the partners to shape firm-level decisions, and can move between closing an LP, setting the quarter’s priorities with the partners, and running a founder event in the same week.

Investor Relations
Drive the operations of the fund's next raise. Own the operational process end to end - pipeline, data room preparation, diligence requests, meeting prep, and follow-up.
Bring in new investor leads through one-on-one meetings and events, and keep every conversation and commitment tracked so nothing gets lost.
Proactively deepen relationships with existing LPs, and lead the writing of investor updates that are clear and concise. 

Financial Operations
Manage internal age1 operations team and part-time operational support such as CFO/fund admin, tax advisors, audit, payroll, subscriptions, etc.
Report firm performance to the relevant databases on an ongoing basis.
Oversee all financial planning, analysis, forecasting, and budgeting.
Ensure end-to-end finance support across the fund lifecycle and portfolio deal activity

Portfolio Relationship Management
Own the relationships and ongoing communication with portfolio companies.
Lead the growth of age1’s platform for portfolio support - helping founders hire, raise subsequent rounds, and access the resources and networks that give them an edge. Build repeatable programs founders across the portfolio can draw on.

Sourcing, Diligence, and Community
Lead the firm’s community efforts, own the CRM, and support sourcing. This can take many forms: spearhead media, curate and host events, or plan a founder program/fellowship. 
Support the investment team in making efficient, maximally-informed decisions, with an emphasis on portfolio construction and modeling. 
Find and build the non-obvious paths to activate age1’s network with outsized impact.  For a path towards Partner, build a track record of contributing directly to investment decisions, with an emphasis on portfolio construction and modeling.

Incubations
Help lead company formation for NewCo incubations in their 0 to 1 phase, owning set-up of operational platforms: entity registration, standing up finances, establishing governance, etc.
Help drive negotiation of key agreements linked to the NewCo’s vision for assets or partnerships (investment terms, legal documents, and BD/transactions).
Help set NewCo vision, and on a path toward Partner, build a track record in contributing to the recruitment of key founding hires plus the production of fundraising materials (e.g., NewCo deck).

Fund Strategy
Contribute to setting fund priorities and high-level firm initiatives alongside the partners.
Shape how the firm allocates time, capital, and attention as it scales.

Team Growth and Firm Operations
Work with the partners to set and execute team development goals.
Manage the physical office, website, public relations, and community events; own the recruiting process for summer interns and fellows.

Attributes We're Looking For

You have a great read on people . Building community, you know exactly who to route to the partners. With LPs, co-investors, and portfolio companies, you have a sharp instinct for what they need and how they're feeling.
Operational excellence: nothing drops . You cross the t's and dot the i's without being asked. Things don’t slip despite every best intention of the GP’s chaos. You keep the trains running on time with little oversight, and you're skilled at managing up.
You build systems with judgment, not just to-do lists . You've owned complex, cross-functional work with minimal existing infrastructure and turned informal processes into things that scale. You can make the call without waiting for detailed instructions.
No job is beneath you or above you, uninteresting, or out of your abilities . You are happy subbing in wherever the firm needs it, and you don't see logistical execution as separate from senior operating work. You like organizing events (even if it means last minute Uber Eats-ing drinks or a whiteboard) and you don’t mind supporting portfolio companies with ops, such as helping them file documents or set up payroll.
You’re financially fluent . Budgeting, forecasting, and management reporting are comfortable territory, and you can hold your own on fund mechanics.
You write well . You produce concise, high-quality materials for investors, founders, and senior stakeholders, and you default to clear written communication.
You can push back . Low ego, high confidence, and high integrity - you execute the partners' vision and you have the conviction to tell them when you think they're wrong.
You care about the mission . You have a passion for longevity and biotech, and are invested in the future of the fund.

Why You May Not Be a Fit

You want a narrowly defined role with stable, predictable responsibilities.
You're most comfortable operating inside mature systems someone else built.
You want to advise on operations without being accountable for implementation.
You need frequent partner direction to prioritize and finish work.
You see administrative or logistical execution as beneath a senior operating role.
You add process for its own sake, without asking if it improves speed or judgment.

Job Summary

Iambic Therapeutics is seeking a Senior or Executive Director to lead the analytical development and QC function within CMC. This leadership role will provide scientific, strategic, and operational oversight of Analytical Development and Quality Control activities across Iambic’s small-molecule portfolio, supporting programs from early clinical development through late-stage development and commercialization. The individual will lead phase-appropriate analytical strategies for drug substance and drug product, including analytical method development, transfer and validation, specifications, impurity control, stability, reference standards, product characterization, and release testing. The role will serve as the primary Analytical Development/QC lead for internal cross-functional teams and external CDMOs/testing labs, ensuring high-quality, compliant, and timely execution of analytical activities in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and company procedures.

Key Responsibilities

Lead DS and DP analytical strategy and scientific oversight across characterization, impurity and degradation-product control, reference standards, comparability, and stability, with responsibility for shelf-life/retest assessment and emerging stability risks.
Lead analytical method development, validation, transfer, lifecycle management, and troubleshooting across DS and DP, ensuring methods are fit for purpose, scientifically sound, and aligned with regulatory expectations.
Oversee QC testing and data review for release and stability, including OOS/OOT investigations, deviations, root-cause assessment, CAPAs, and resolution of analytical issues.
Establish scientifically justified specifications and analytical acceptance criteria based on product and process understanding, batch history, stability data, and stage of development.
Provide analytical leadership for dissolution and product-performance testing, including development of QC and discriminatory methods for oral drug products.
Lead the outsourced analytical and QC network, including partner selection, technical oversight, governance, issue resolution, and performance management.
Ensure analytical activities support program timelines and manufacturing readiness through close partnership with Drug Substance, Drug Product, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Clinical Supply, and other cross-functional teams.
Lead analytical CMC support for global regulatory submissions and health authority interactions, including authoring and review of relevant Module 3 content, specifications and justifications, analytical methods, stability sections, and responses to regulatory queries.
Recruit, lead, coach, and develop team members; oversee functional resource planning and budget proposals; and foster a collaborative, high-performing environment aligned with organizational goals.

Qualifications

Ph.D. in Analytical Chemistry or a related field with 12+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical/Biotech industry (or an M.Sc. with 14+ years or B.Sc. with 17+ years of experience).
Extensive hands-on experience in analytical method development, transfer, troubleshooting, and validation for small molecule drug substance (DS) and drug product (DP) across early and late-stage development.
Strong experience developing phase-appropriate analytical control strategies, including specifications, impurity/degradation-product control, reference standards, stability-indicating methods, dissolution, and product characterization.
Demonstrated experience supporting early and late-stage development and regulatory filings, including IND/IMPD and preferably NDA/MAA.
Proven success leading Analytical Development and QC activities through external CDMOs, including technical oversight, issue resolution, and management of multiple programs and partners.

Proven leadership experience in building collaborative, high-performing teams and working effectively across Drug Substance, Drug Product, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Clinical Supply, and other functions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical issues, risks, and recommendations to internal stakeholders, external partners, and health authorities.

The CITY COLLEGE of NEW YORK

The Executive Director will provide strategic leadership for AI-BIOME, an NSF-funded Programmable Cloud Laboratory (PCL) headquartered at the CUNY City College of New York (CCNY) and the CUNY Advanced Science Research Center (ASRC). Working closely with the AI-BIOME Co-Directors, 5 PIs, Science; AI and Data Leads, CCNY and ASRC leadership, and partner institutions including Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL), 30+ partners from industry, the Executive Director will establish AI-BIOME as a national research resource for state-of-the-art AI research enabling distributed scientific discovery in the area of bio-inspired materials and molecular materials engineering.

The Executive Director will lead the strategic growth, external partnerships, organizational development, and long-term sustainability of AI-BIOME while fostering integration with CCNY and ASRC interdisciplinary research programs and core facilities. Working in partnership with the Director of Operations, the Executive Director will ensure successful execution of AI-BIOME's research, education, workforce development, innovation, and outreach missions.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Program Development

Partner with the AI-BIOME Co-Directors and Executive Committee to develop and implement AI-BIOME's strategic vision.
Coordinate with the AI-BIOME Science, AI and Data Leads to align with NSF TIP’s vision for PCL on these three focus areas.
Translate scientific priorities into organizational strategy, operational priorities, and measurable milestones.
Identify opportunities for program growth, strategic partnerships, new funding, and long-term sustainability.
Lead strategic planning and organizational development across research, education, workforce development, innovation, and outreach.

Institutional Partnerships & External Relations

Represent AI-BIOME with NSF, federal agencies, City and State agencies, partner institutions, industry, philanthropic organizations, and government stakeholders.
Develop strategic partnerships with universities, national laboratories, industry, and community organizations.
Build AI-BIOME's national and international visibility and contribute to the development of the emerging Programmable Cloud Laboratory ecosystem.
Support technology transfer, entrepreneurship, and commercialization activities in collaboration with institutional partners.

Integration with CCNY & ASRC Research Infrastructure

Work closely with CCNY and ASRC leadership to integrate AI-BIOME with interdisciplinary research initiatives and shared research infrastructure.
Develop new opportunities that leverage the CCNY and ASRC core facilities in laboratory automation, high-throughput experimentation, materials characterization, photonics, imaging, computation, and data science.
Foster collaborations that expand utilization of shared research infrastructure and strengthen AI-BIOME as a hub for interdisciplinary discovery.

Organizational Leadership

Provide leadership and mentorship to senior staff.
Foster a collaborative, innovative, and inclusive organizational culture across AI-BIOME's multi-institutional community.
Work closely with the Director of Operations to ensure efficient implementation of organizational priorities.

Program Oversight

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR - Converse County Aging Services

(CCAS) Douglas & Glenrock, Wyoming

Full-Time | Starting at $80,000

YOUR NEXT LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY COULD TAKE YOU SOMEWHERE YOU ACTUALLY WANT TO LIVE.

What if your next career move came with wide-open spaces, small-town community, outdoor adventure, and the opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of older adults and families?

Converse County Aging Services (CCAS) is seeking an experienced, strategic, compassionate Executive Director to lead our organization and its senior services operations in Douglas and Glenrock, Wyoming.

This is a high-level nonprofit executive leadership opportunity for someone who is ready to lead people, strengthen operations, oversee senior center services and programs, work closely with a Board of Directors, build community partnerships, and help shape the future of aging services throughout Converse County.

The Executive Director will provide leadership across the organization while ensuring that CCAS remains a welcoming, responsive, financially sustainable, and community-centered resource for older adults, caregivers, families, volunteers, and community members.

And yes—you'll have to get used to seeing a jackalope around town. ;)

About Converse County Aging Services

CCAS is more than an organization that provides services to older adults.

Our senior centers are part of the community.

They are places where people gather, connect, share meals, participate in activities and programs, access resources, build friendships, and remain engaged in the communities they call home.

CCAS provides important senior services, aging services, community programs, nutrition services, activities, resources, and support for older adults throughout Converse County.

The Executive Director plays an important role in making sure these services continue to meet the changing needs of the community.

This means understanding the big picture while also appreciating the day-to-day realities of senior center operations—including staff leadership, programs and activities, facilities, service delivery, community engagement, partnerships, compliance, budgeting, and the experience of the people CCAS serves.

We're looking for a leader who understands that successful aging services are about more than programs on paper.

They're about people, relationships, connection, dignity, independence, and community.

WHY CONVERSE COUNTY?

If you're looking for a place where community still means something, Converse County might be your kind of place.

Douglas and Glenrock offer the best of small-town Wyoming: friendly communities, room to breathe, beautiful scenery, and plenty to do without giving up the convenience of being within reach of larger Wyoming communities.

LOVE THE OUTDOORS?

You're going to have plenty to explore.

Converse County offers opportunities for hiking, fishing, camping, hunting, boating, biking, and simply getting outside.

LOVE HISTORY?

There's plenty of that, too.

Explore historic sites, museums, railroad history, and the many stories of the American West that shaped the area.

HAVE A FAMILY?

Converse County offers parks, walking paths, community events, museums, water activities, and plenty of opportunities to get outside together.

LIKE A LITTLE WYOMING TRADITION?

Douglas is home to the Wyoming State Fair & Rodeo, and the community celebrates its famous jackalope with the kind of small-town personality that makes Wyoming special.

Now About The Job...

We're looking for a leader who can take the big-picture executive view while understanding the details that make senior services and community operations successful.

The Executive Director Will

Provide strategic leadership for Converse County Aging Services and its mission to serve older adults and the community.

Partner with the Board of Directors on governance, organizational strategy, policy, and long-term direction.

Lead, support, and develop the organization's leadership team and staff.

Provide executive oversight of senior center operations in Douglas and Glenrock, including programs, services, facilities, staffing, and community activities.

Ensure senior center programs and services are responsive to the needs of older adults, caregivers, families, and the broader community.

Oversee organizational compliance, risk management, policies, contracts, service agreements, and regulatory requirements.

Work closely with Finance & Administration leadership on budgets, financial reporting, grants, cash flow, internal controls, and long-term financial sustainability.

Support program leadership and promote high-quality, person-centered service delivery.

Help ensure CCAS facilities and senior centers remain safe, welcoming, accessible, and community-focused.

Build strong relationships with community partners, healthcare organizations, local governments, funding agencies, donors, volunteers, businesses, and other stakeholders.

Represent CCAS as a visible and engaged leader throughout Converse County.

Advocate for the needs and interests of older adults and aging communities.

Develop strong organizational systems, processes, and accountability measures.

Identify opportunities to strengthen programs, services, partnerships, funding, and community engagement.

Help position CCAS for long-term growth, sustainability, and continued community impact.

SENIOR CENTER & COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP

This position requires more than traditional administrative leadership.

The Executive Director should understand what it takes to operate a successful senior center and community-based aging services organization.

That Includes Recognizing The Importance Of

Creating welcoming and inclusive senior center environments.

Supporting meaningful programs, activities, meals, social opportunities, and community connections.

Understanding the operational needs of multiple locations.

Supporting staff who work directly with older adults and community members.

Maintaining strong relationships with participants, families, volunteers, and community partners.

Responding to changing demographics and the evolving needs of older adults.

Balancing mission, service quality, financial responsibility, and operational sustainability.

Ensuring CCAS remains a trusted and visible part of the Converse County community.

The right Executive Director will be comfortable moving between boardroom strategy and community connection—from reviewing a budget or grant proposal to visiting a senior center, talking with staff, meeting with community partners, or listening to the people CCAS serves.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR AN EXECUTIVE-LEVEL LEADER

This isn't a position for someone who wants to simply keep the wheels turning.

We're looking for someone who can lead, plan, make decisions, develop people, understand the numbers, manage complexity, strengthen operations, and build relationships.

You Should Bring

Strong executive leadership and communication skills.

Strategic thinking and organizational planning abilities.

Financial literacy and comfort with budgets, financial reports, grants, and organizational finances.

Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills.

Experience leading teams and organizational operations.

Experience with nonprofit, human services, senior services, healthcare, community services, or a related organization is highly valued.

An understanding of senior center operations, aging services, community-based services, or programs serving older adults is preferred.

Excellent relationship-building and community engagement skills.

Professionalism, integrity, accountability, and sound judgment.

A genuine commitment to serving older adults, supporting independence, and strengthening communities.

A Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Human Services, Gerontology, Social Services, or a related field is preferred, along with 3-5 years of leadership or management experience. Equivalent leadership experience may be considered.

THIS IS A CHANCE TO MAKE A VISIBLE DIFFERENCE

At CCAS, leadership isn't happening somewhere far removed from the people being served.

It's happening in the senior centers, programs, community gatherings, partnerships, conversations, and everyday interactions that help older adults remain connected and engaged.

As Executive Director, you'll have the opportunity to shape an organization that has a direct and visible impact on the people of Converse County.

You'll lead an established community organization while helping determine what aging services and senior center programs should look like for the future.

Compensation & Benefits

Starting salary: $80,000 annually, with consideration given to experience and qualifications.

CCAS Offers

Paid Time Off (PTO)

Paid Sick Leave

Medical insurance - employee portion paid by CCAS

Wyoming retirement pension

Additional Benefits In Accordance With CCAS Policies

Relocation assistance may be available

READY FOR A DIFFERENT KIND OF LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY?

Maybe you're ready to trade traffic for open roads.

Maybe you're ready for a community where people know their neighbors.

Maybe you're looking for a nonprofit executive leadership position where your work has a visible impact on the lives of older adults and the community.

Maybe you're looking for a place where your leadership can actually make a difference.

Or maybe you just want to live somewhere you can finish work and be five minutes from wide-open Wyoming.

Whatever brings you here, you'll find an opportunity to lead an organization with a meaningful mission, support senior services and community programs, and become part of a community that values its people.

COME LEAD CCAS. COME EXPERIENCE CONVERSE COUNTY. COME SEE WHAT WYOMING HAS TO OFFER.

Job Description

What’s it like working for a company where you are treated as more than a number? Empowering. Joining our IT Program Management team means you are the backbone behind managing all the technology aspects for multiple contracts and programs that help keep nations safe. With the diversity of our offerings and work, you’ll get to take on new challenges while your career reaches new heights.

BAE is looking for an experienced Program Manager (PGM) to manage a complex, enterprise impacting Global Trade technology program. The role will report into our IT Program Management Office (PMO), with deep engagement with stakeholders across BAE Systems business sectors. The PGM will be responsible for end to end execution of the Global Trade Technology Program, managing matrixed IT teams.

The candidate will have strong program management experience managing multiple concurrent programs with several projects rolling up under each of the program. The candidate will be leading programs and projects through the project lifecycle including Planning and Analysis, Execution, Delivery, Stabilization and Benefit Realization.

Required Education, Experience, & Skills

Program leadership in this role will include:

Business case development.
Effective design and development of Portfolio, Program, Project (P3) execution strategies.
Cross boundary integration, dependency identification & tracking.
Effective leadership and program & project execution.
Develop solutions to complex problems which require use of ingenuity, innovation and robust design.
Management of requirements, priorities and alignment with organizational objectives & success criteria.
Work breakdown structure, effort estimation, resource loaded schedule management and execution to the strategy/plan, proactive risk identification and mitigation,
Team leadership including guiding and motivating team members,
Cost breakdown structure, cost estimation, cost management throughout the project lifecycle including management of cost overrun/underrun.
Quality / Test Management.
Vendor relationship management including working with third-party systems integrators
Organizational change management, communication, training, stakeholder engagement, enablement.

The candidate shall be highly customer focused, meeting customer expectation and responsive to feedback. The ideal candidate will have experience in both IT and in leading complex business facing initiatives with the ability to drive technology adoption within BAE Systems business sectors. The candidate shall leverage servant leadership, emotional intelligence, strong communication and decision making skills to navigate effectively across all functional areas and organizational levels.

Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills

Experience driving enterprise standardization and transformation, with accountability to the executive level.
PMP Certification.
Agile Certification.
Aerospace & defense technology experience and familiarity with global trade concepts.

Pay Information

Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.

About BAE Systems, Inc.

BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is an ambitious mission, but it’s what we do at BAE Systems. Working here means using your passion and ingenuity where it counts – defending national security with breakthrough technology, superior products, and intelligence solutions. As you develop the latest technology and defend national security, you will continually hone your skills on a team—making a big impact on a global scale. At BAE Systems, you’ll find a rewarding career that truly makes a difference.
